text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The newspaper says that the government might move to remove the director general of the state- run Kaunas alcohol producer Stumbras Algimantas Dzhiugas during the general shareholders' meeting on April 5. The company is alleged to have been involved in illegal dealings with alcohol.

- The indepenent Belarus newspaper Narodnaja Volia was forced by President Alexander Lukashenko administration's to move to Vilnius once again. The editor-in-chief Josif Seredich said that journalism was one of the most dangerous professions in Belarus now. The newspaper is published in the Lietuvos rytas publishing house.

- The Lithuanian parliament has submitted two draft laws on banking. If passed, the Lithuanian State Commercial Bank and the Agricultural Bank will be privatised and the troubled Innovation bank will be liquidated.

- Ignalina nuclear power plant's first reactor will be brought back on line after 70 days planned maintenance works which start on April 1 despite the recommendations of the international expert panel to close it until additional security measures have been put in place.

- The state run Savings Bank said on Tuesday it had 30 million litas net profit in 1996 versus 39 million litas losses a year before. The net profit of the bank is the highest so far among the country's commercial banks.
- The prosecutor's office appealed to the court to get Tauro Bankas to pay 6.67 million litas in damages.
- Swedish Justice Minister Laila Freivalds who is on a two days visit to Vilnius refused to comment on an attempted assaination on the eve of the trip.

- The popularity of Lithuania's President Algirdas Brazauskas and Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius continued to grow in March, Baltic Survey's people opinion poll showed. Their popularity was up by seven percent in a month.
- Parliament's legal comittee will have to decide whether to submit the candidature of Kazys Ednychia as prosecutor general for parliament consideration.
- The Centre Union and Liberal parties are likely to form a coalition in Vilnius council.
- Preliminary data shows that the Lithuanian Polish election action candidate Jan Senkevich was elected to parliament during run off elections held with the local elections last Sunday.

- The 1996 results of the banks contradicted expectations that international audits would show that the banks were in a more serious situation than thought. Most banks increased their profits last year.
- The Bank of Lithuania suspended the Suprema brokerage house from buying government T-bills for six months after the broker made bids in an auction but failed to transfer the money.
